_comment: Annotated maps shown by the demo. Each entry points to a map file in this folder; "story" marks maps that also have a narrative; "page" is the map's own page, built by scripts/build_pages.py (the Miller sheet has none: its texts are illustrative). The 144-map collection is in collection.json, generated by scripts/build_collection.py.

title.la: Tartariae sive Magni Chami regni typus
title.en: Map of Tartary, or of the Kingdom of the Great Khan

maps.creator: Abraham Ortelius
maps.repository: Boston Public Library, via Internet Archive
maps.summary: Reading edition. All 40 texts engraved on the map, and Ortelius's description of Tartary printed on the back, each in Latin as engraved, with abbreviations written out and an English translation. Read from the scan by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5) and scored against the published edition.

maps.creator: Jodocus Hondius
maps.repository: Map: HKUST Library; text pages: Utrecht University Library
maps.summary: Reading edition. The 100 texts on the map (the address to the reader, notes on Gog and Magog, the tombs of the khans, Christian Tenduc, the Great Wall and asbestos, and the names of peoples and seas) and 323 place names, and the atlas's description of Tartary on pp. 333–334, in Latin and English. Read from the scans by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5); the description was compared with the project team's transcription, each difference checked on the scan by the AI.

maps.creator: Cornelis de Jode
maps.repository: Map: HKUST Library; text pages: Bibliothèque nationale de France
maps.summary: Reading edition. The 56 texts on the map (the four roundel captions from Jesuit reports, notes on the Great Wall, musk, Japan and Chinese learning, and the names of regions and peoples) and 314 place names, read from the HKUST copy by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5), with the project team's own reading beside it where there is one; and the description “China quae et Sina” on the back, in the team's transcription and translation.

maps.creator: Abraham Ortelius, after Anthony Jenkinson
maps.repository: Map: David Rumsey Map Collection; text page: Biblioteca Nacional de España
maps.summary: Reading edition. The 63 texts on Jenkinson's map (Ivan IV, the golden idol Zlata Baba, the horde turned to stone, the Kirghiz, Samarkand and the road to Cathay) and 205 place names, read from the David Rumsey Map Collection copy by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5) and compared with van den Broecke's edition; and Ortelius's description of Russia on the back, from the 1595 Latin edition.

title.en: Tartary, or the Empire of the Great Khan

maps.creator: Willem Janszoon Blaeu
maps.repository: Map: David Rumsey Map Collection; text pages: Biblioteca Nacional de España
maps.summary: Reading edition. The 69 texts on the map (Gog and Magog, Christian Tenduc, the tombs of the khans, Cambalu, the Great Wall) and 386 place names, read from the David Rumsey Map Collection copy by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5); and the atlas's description of Tartary on the back, from the Biblioteca Nacional de España copy.

maps.creator: John Speed, engraved by Dirck Grijp
maps.repository: Bibliothèque nationale de France, via Wikimedia Commons
maps.summary: Reading edition. All 43 texts on the map (title, town views, costume figures and 26 notes, from the Dutch voyages to Nova Zembla to the Great Wall) and Speed's description of Tartary printed on the back, each as engraved or printed and in modern spelling. Read from the scan by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5); the passages checked against the scan match word for word.

title.fr: Carte generale de la Siberie et de la Grande Tartarie
title.en: General map of Siberia and Great Tartary

maps.creator: French copy of a lost Russian map
maps.repository: Newberry Library, Chicago (Ayer MS map 30, sheet 115)
maps.summary: Reading edition. A Russian map of Siberia known only from this French manuscript copy: the Russian names written in French, and the tents of the Yakuts, Tungus, Kalmyks and Mongols. Its notes, peoples and regions are pinned on the map, and its 264 towns, rivers and lakes can be shown on demand, each as written and in English. Read from the scan by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5); the faded scan has its contrast adjusted, with the original one click away.

title.zh: 米勒地圖集 第四葉
title.en: Nautical Atlas of the World (Miller Atlas), folio 4

maps.creator: Lopo Homem, Pedro and Jorge Reinel; illuminated by António de Holanda
maps.repository: Bibliothèque nationale de France (via Library of Congress / World Digital Library)
maps.summary: Feature demonstration, September 2026: transcriptions and translations are illustrative. A vellum sheet painted on both sides: the recto shows the Magnus Sinus (the Great Gulf of the Chinese sea), the verso the China Sea with the Moluccas. Latin cartouches on both faces.
